newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UK energy minister promotes UK gas model for Europe.
newsitem.headline: UK energy minister promotes UK gas model for Europe.

text.p: Britain's Energy Minister will on Monday urge the European Union to copy the British approach to gas market liberalisation.

Gas is growing in popularity, discoveries offer abundant supplies and the Europe-wide gas network is expanding, Lord Fraser said in a precis issued in advance of his speech to businessmen and academics at Leiden University later on Monday.
The key to competitiveness was market liberalisation and that rested on four key conditions, Fraser said.

"The four points I have in mind are: the separation of the functions of transportation and supply; non-discrimination in terms of supply; transparency of pricing for use of the pipeline system; (and) an effective, independent, regulatory authority," he said.
Fraser believed discussions within the European Union were not focused on these points.

"Without any one of them - and this is the situation we see the current European discussions coming perilously near - there is a strong risk that the whole process will lead to disappointment and frustration," he said.

Britain has led the way in opening up its gas market to competition. But not all EU countries agree on the pace and extent of liberalisation, with some, such as France, wanting to retain some form of price control.
Britain also expects to be a net exporter of gas from 1998 when the Interconnector pipeline linking England to continental Europe opens.
